summary: A Forest Service lookout near Augusta, first used in the 1920s, with an L-4 cab from 1931 and the present R-6 cab from 1968, staffed each summer.

facts.design: Present R-6 flat cab, built 1968; earlier L-4 cab built 1931

access.note: Staffed Forest Service lookout. No source read describes a road or trail to the site or says whether the public may visit.

events.note: L-4 cab built, per the register and firelookout.com; a 9 July 1931 newspaper item reports the station under construction
Newspaper item of August 1940 mentions a lookout at the station
Present R-6 flat cab built 1968; the register describes it as the present cab
University of Montana student served as volunteer lookout that summer (Sun Valley Sun item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com both give 1931 for an L-4 cab and 1968 for the present R-6 cab. The two dates describe two cabs on the same site, which is why the record shows a conflict.
The register gives 8,793 ft (2,680 m), matching the record's 2680.1 m; firelookout.com gives 8858 ft. The sources do not explain the difference.

sources.title: Montana fire lookouts: Alone on a peak to watch for wildfires

notes_for_editor: The 1931 and 1968 cabs are both real per the register and firelookout.com, so the record's build-year conflict is two cabs, not an error. The 1940 and 1984 staffing items come from a Montana lookout-history page quoting old newspapers; I did not see the newspapers. The KTVH article carries no date in the cached copy, so 'five lookouts' is undated. Access is unconfirmed: OpenStreetMap tags the structure access=private (from the record; not read here). No rental listing found; search recreation.gov directly before saying more. No notable fires found. No new photos. 2026-10-08 check: the 9 July 1931, 15 August 1940 and 16 August 1984 dates and the forest name were confirmed on the Forest Lookouts page and added to the evidence record; the story text is unchanged.
